Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
150 PM EDT Sat Aug 15 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 134 PM EDT Saturday...

Beneficial rainfall increasingly likely Sunday night into early
Monday morning. Amounts near 1" possible in Vermont's Northeast
Kingdom. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 134 PM EDT Saturday...

1. Pleasant conditions through the daylight hours Sunday, then
widespread showers with moderate, beneficial rainfall Sunday
night into Monday morning. 

2. Near seasonable temperatures are expected next week, with 
chances for showers and thunderstorms mid-week as a cold front moves 
through the region. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 134 PM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Large area of high pressure (1025 mb) centered
over sern Ontario will remain our controlling weather feature
tonight and through the daylight hours on Sunday. Daytime flat
cumulus field this afternoon will give way to mostly clear and
light wind conditions tonight. While some high clouds move in
late across nrn NY, conditions once again appear favorable for
locally dense fog 06-12Z east of the Green Mountains in Vermont.
Good radiational cooling conditions overall, with overnight lows
mainly in the 40s, except low-mid 50s in the immediate Champlain
Valley. PoPs NIL overnight. 

PBL winds switch light southerly Sunday as sfc anticyclone 
shifts to the Gulf of Maine. Channeled flow will yield somewhat
stronger winds over Lake Champlain of 10-15 kt. This will allow
for slightly warmer afternoon highs in the upper 70s to lower 
80s. Humidity remains modest though, with 2-m dewpoints 
generally in the mid-upper 50s. 

Modest 850-500mb height falls and weak sfc low/frontal system
bring increasing clouds and widespread showers for Sunday night
into early Monday. Rainfall amounts generally 0.25-0.50" with
this system...and generally beneficial. With that said, some of
the statistical guidance, including the probability matched mean
(PMM) QPF from the REFS indicates potential for around 1"
rainfall from Jay Peak eastward across the Northeast Kingdom.
Still not enough to cause any hydro/flooding concerns, but 
highest rainfall totals appear likely in the NEK aided by modest
low-level frontogenesis forcing. Drier conditions return Monday
night into Tuesday with high pressure. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: Heading into the middle of next week, guidance continues 
to show broad cyclonic flow dominating the region, with a frontal 
boundary pushing through sometime Wednesday night into Thursday. 
This front will bring increased shower and thunderstorms, although 
there's still a little uncertainty regarding the details at this 
time range, especially with how long showers linger across the area. 
After this system, a period of drier weather looks to return for the 
latter half of the week. High temperatures for next week will 
gradually trend back towards the 70s areawide after a few days in 
the upper 70s to low 80s earlier in the week. Overall, a period of 
rather unimpactful and seasonable weather is expected for much of 
next week.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 18Z Sunday...VFR conditions are expected to prevail through
most of the forecast period. Winds this afternoon continue to be
north/northwesterly between 5 and 10 knots, although a few gusts
closer to 20 knots are possible throughout the afternoon. Winds look
to trend light and terrain-driven this evening. Some fog development
is expected again tonight, which would be the only exception to VFR
conditions throughout the forecast period. Radiational fog is
expected at the more favored terminals of KMPV and KSLK, and
possibly KEFK as well. The duration of IFR or lower conditions looks
shorter at KSLK in comparison to previous days, generally 8Z to 12Z
with some high clouds expected to stream into the region tonight.
Once fog dissipates tomorrow morning, around 12Z or so, VFR will
prevail for the remainder of the forecast period with dry weather
continuing.

Outlook...

Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Definite
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Likely
SHRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
